title: Rumour: two 3,000+ piece LEGO Architecture sets tipped for 2027
summary: Leaked set numbers suggest LEGO Architecture could follow its record-breaking Sagrada Família with two more large-scale builds in early 2027. Nothing is confirmed yet, and the source remains unproven.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to unverified online leaks, two upcoming LEGO Architecture sets — numbered 21070 and 21071 — could be on the way in 2027. The claims suggest 21070 might arrive in March with 3,142 pieces, followed by 21071 in April with 3,333 pieces. No names, images, pricing or box art have surfaced, and neither LEGO nor Brick Fanatics has confirmed any of this.

The rumour comes from an Instagram leaker whose track record is still considered unproven, though it has been picked up by other leak-focused accounts. If accurate, these would sit just behind LEGO's biggest ever Architecture release — the 12,060-piece 21065 Sagrada Família, due this November — as well as Notre-Dame de Paris, Tower Bridge and Neuschwanstein Castle in terms of scale.

## Why it matters
LEGO Architecture has increasingly leaned into huge, display-worthy builds, and UK fans of large-scale sets, stadium-style projects and premium displays tend to pay close attention to this theme. Even as a rumour, it hints at where the theme might be heading next — bigger, more ambitious landmark builds rather than smaller starter sets.

## What to watch next
As always with early leaks, treat the piece counts and dates as speculative until LEGO or a more established source confirms details. Watch for official set reveals, box art leaks, or retailer listings closer to early 2027 for firmer confirmation.

title: LEGO Harry Potter Ministry of Magic: Comparing the 2022 and 2026 Sets
summary: With 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition due later this month, we look at how it stacks up against the original 2022 modular version.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO is set to release 76476 The Ministry of Magic Collectors' Edition later this month, only the second time this Harry Potter location has been recreated in brick form. The original, 76403 The Ministry of Magic, launched back in 2022 with 990 pieces, a modular multi-level design, nine minifigures, and a price of £89.99. It's since been retired.

The new Collectors' Edition set is a huge step up, coming in at 3,491 pieces — nearly four times the piece count of its predecessor. According to Brick Fanatics, its scale and style appear to take inspiration from 76417 Gringotts Wizarding Bank Collectors' Edition, another large-scale Wizarding World release.

## Why it matters
For Harry Potter fans and collectors, this comparison shows just how far LEGO's approach to iconic movie locations has evolved in a few short years, moving from smaller playable modulars to premium, display-focused Collectors' Edition sets. It's a useful reference point for anyone deciding whether to pick up the new set or hold onto the original.

title: LEGO X-Files GWP stock disappears in the UK
summary: The free 40896 Scully's Lab set that came with LEGO Ideas 21369 The X-Files has now sold out in the UK, following similar shortages across Europe.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
LEGO Insiders in the UK who were hoping to grab the free 40896 The X-Files: Scully's Lab alongside the new 21369 The X-Files LEGO Ideas set are currently out of luck, as UK stock of the 221-piece GWP has run dry.

The promotion originally gave early access to Insiders members from 1–3 August, pairing the 1,478-piece 21369 The X-Files set with the exclusive Scully's Lab build, which includes an examination table, sink, cupboards, accessories and a Dana Scully minifigure.

The GWP had already vanished across Europe due to high demand, and it now appears the UK has followed suit, leaving the US as the only region with confirmed stock at the time of writing, according to Brick Fanatics. The offer is officially scheduled to run until 10 August, though it looks likely supplies will run out well before then.

Meanwhile, 21369 The X-Files itself is proving hugely popular, with the £179.99 set already on back order in the UK, US and Europe, with some delivery estimates stretching into October 2026.

## Why it matters
GWPs (gifts with purchase) are a big draw for LEGO Ideas fans and collectors, and losing access to an exclusive build like this can be frustrating for UK buyers who missed the early window. It's also a reminder of just how in-demand X-Files-themed LEGO has proven to be, which could affect availability and secondary market prices for anyone still hoping to complete the set.

## What to watch next

title: LEGO Ideas: Autumn Forest and The Fountain Place hit 10K supporters
summary: Two more fan-designed builds have crossed the 10,000-supporter line in LEGO Ideas' second 2026 review, joining a growing shortlist of projects hoping to become official sets.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
According to Brick Fanatics, two new fan creations have reached the crucial 10,000-supporter milestone in the current LEGO Ideas review window.

**Autumn Forest**, designed by CoasterZoom, is a 4,891-piece modular woodland scene that appears inspired by the official set 11372 Autumn Cottage Garden. It stands over 42cm tall and includes a mix of tree types - weeping willow, birch, poplar, oak and beech among them - alongside pebble paths designed for minifigures to wander through.

**The Fountain Place**, from designer Santheg, is a 2,978-piece modular building that began life as a simple flower shop concept before evolving into a fuller scene. It features 'The Potted Brick' flower shop at ground level, a fountain with an angel statue, and 'Stone's Throw Photography' studio upstairs, plus a delivery truck and several named minifigures.

Both models now join 64 other projects already sitting in the second LEGO Ideas review of 2026, all awaiting a decision on whether they'll be turned into official retail sets.

## Why it matters
Reaching 10,000 supporters doesn't guarantee a set - it simply earns a place in the review process, where the LEGO Group's Ideas team decides what actually gets made. Still, for fans who enjoy modular builds, detailed dioramas and display-friendly designs, tracking which projects clear this hurdle is a good way to spot potential future sets long before any official announcement.

## What to watch next
There's roughly a month left for further submissions to reach 10K before this review period closes. Worth keeping an eye on Brick Fanatics and the official LEGO Ideas site for the next names to join the list - and, eventually, which of the 66+ qualifying projects the LEGO Group actually chooses to review and greenlight.

title: New LEGO DC set highlights Batman and Superman's grip on the theme
summary: The newly revealed 40859 Golden Age Superman and Batman Figures set is a welcome nod to the Man of Steel, but it also underlines how narrow LEGO DC's focus has become this decade.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Brick Fanatics reports that LEGO has revealed 40859 Golden Age Superman and Batman Figures, a set due to launch on 1 September featuring both heroes in their classic 1950s comic-book looks.

While fans will likely enjoy seeing Superman get some rare spotlight, the set also reinforces a wider pattern: according to the source, almost every LEGO DC release since 2020 has centred on Batman, Superman, or both. The only exception this decade has reportedly been 76157 Wonder Woman vs. Cheetah, released back in April 2020.

Superman himself has had a patchy run. After 2018's 76096 Superman & Krypto Team-Up, the character was absent from sets for seven years until 76302 Superman vs. Lex Luthor arrived in January 2025 - only for that set to retire before the year was out, per the source.

This is a notable contrast to 2018, when LEGO DC included heroes and villains like Aquaman, Black Manta, Supergirl, Brainiac and Nightwing across multiple sets, showing a broader roster than what's on offer today.

## Why it matters
For collectors and fans who want more variety from LEGO DC, this trend matters because it suggests the wider DC Universe - Aquaman, Wonder Woman, Green Lantern and others - is being sidelined in favour of the two most recognisable heroes. If you're building a DC display or hoping for specific characters, it's worth knowing that Batman and Superman currently dominate new releases.

## What to watch next
It remains to be seen whether upcoming LEGO DC sets will branch out beyond Gotham and Metropolis, or whether Batman and Superman will continue to be the default focus. Nothing here is confirmed as a permanent shift, and it is presented by the source as an observed trend, not an official LEGO statement about future strategy.

title: Andrew Garfield surprised by his own $15,000 rare LEGO Spider-Man minifigure
summary: A 2013 San Diego Comic-Con exclusive LEGO minifigure of Andrew Garfield's Spider-Man now fetches around $15,000 on the secondary market, and the actor himself hadn't even seen it until now.
bodyMarkdown:
## What happened
Actor Andrew Garfield, who played Spider-Man in three films between 2012 and 2021, was shown his own ultra-rare LEGO minifigure for the first time in a clip shared by content creator MiniSuperHerosToday. The figure was originally a 2013 San Diego Comic-Con exclusive, limited to just 350 copies and given out via a daily lottery to attendees. These days it typically sells for around $15,000 on the secondary market.

Garfield appeared genuinely unaware that a version of his Spider-Man had ever been made into a LEGO minifigure. Fellow actor Claire Foy, present during the reveal, joked that so few were produced because nobody wanted one.

A more common, mass-produced Andrew Garfield Spider-Man minifigure later appeared in set 76261 Spider-Man Final Battle in 2023, making it far more accessible than the original con-exclusive version.

Meanwhile, current Spider-Man actor Tom Holland has three official LEGO sets tied to Spider-Man: Brand New Day now available: 76346 Spider-Man Hero Figure, 76349 Spider-Man Prison Transport Chase, and 76350 Spider-Man vs. Hulk Epic Clash, priced between £44.99 and £89.99.

76788 Nevermore Academy is bigger, at 890 pieces, and carries a higher price of £59.99 / $69.99 / €69.99. Notably, it includes the only minifigure released so far in the entire LEGO Wednesday theme, making it a must for completists.

## Why it matters
For collectors and display builders, this confirms the "mini landmark plus exclusive minifigure" format isn't tied to Disney licensing alone. If you enjoyed the compact scale and shelf-friendly size of Mini Disney sets, these new Harry Potter and Wednesday releases offer a similar experience, and possibly a template for other themes going forward.

## What to watch next
It's worth watching whether other LEGO licensed themes adopt this same mini-building format, and whether Mini Disney itself ever returns given its multi-year gap since the last release.
